title: toolcall-boundary-preservation-and-progress-checkpoint-resume-handshake-openai-compat
author: Diego Patel
description:
Context: Customers reported two related classes of failures for streaming API users that (1) received partial structured outputs when the client cancelled mid-toolcall and (2) retried/resumed streams that caused duplicate tool invocations or corrupted JSON blobs. Motivation: make client cancel/reconnect/resume semantics safer for structured output and tool/function calling while preserving low-latency behavior for simple text streams. Goals: (a) preserve toolcall boundary integrity — never invoke or commit a toolcall unless a durable boundary/safepoint is reached, (b) allow resumable progress checkpoints for long-lived streams so clients can resume from the last committed checkpoint without re-invoking tools, (c) provide a small handshake protocol extension for resume idempotency tokens and deadline negotiation so client+server can agree on how much work is durable after reconnects, and (d) maintain OpenAI-compat behavior for basic consumers.

This PR implements a runtime + protocol extension plus SDK glue to support "commit checkpoints" embedded in streaming frames. Checkpoints contain a short id (sha1 of recent output frame boundary), an idempotency token for pending toolcalls, and a monotonic progress cursor. Checkpoints are emitted at safe boundaries (end-of-json-object, end-of-toolcall-output, or configured chunk intervals). On client cancel, the server will: (1) attempt to emit a final checkpoint within the cancel grace window, (2) persist checkpoint metadata to the lease/stream metadata store, and (3) abort any uncommitted toolcalls. On client reconnect, clients present the last-known checkpoint id and resume token; the server reconciles and either resumes generation after the checkpoint or rejects resume if the checkpoint is unknown or expired. To avoid duplicate tool invocations we require toolcall boundary confirmation: tool providers must return a call-commit marker; until that marker is persisted the tool is treated as not-yet-committed and will not be replayed on resume.

Compatibility notes: The change is opt-in at the OpenAI compatibility layer via a new header X-Redwood-Resume: checkpoint-id=<id>;token=<tok>. Existing clients continue working unchanged. The Redwood Python and TypeScript SDKs get helpers to surface checkpointing and a small resume() helper that drives the handshake.

Design checklist:
- [x] Define checkpoint frame structure and schema-fingerprint approach (small, compact, stable)
- [x] Emit checkpoints at JSON/toolcall boundaries and on periodic intervals
- [x] Persist checkpoint metadata in stream lease store for 24h (configurable)
- [x] Require toolcall commit markers before commit; introduce transient toolcall state
- [x] Server-side resume handshake with token validation and deadline negotiation
- [x] SDK helpers (py/ts) + examples in quickstarts repo
- [x] E2E tests covering single-client cancel, reconnect+resume, and forced double-invoke prevention
- [x] Metric instrumentation for checkpoint emission rate, resume success rate, duplicate-invoke attempts

What changed (summary of commits):
- Implement stream checkpoint emitter and serializer in serving/runtime/streaming (checkpoint frames, small serializer)
- Add resume token negotiation endpoint and handshake logic in gateway/proxy
- Add transient toolcall state machine and commit-marker handling in runtime/tooling
- Add persistence glue for checkpoint metadata in lease-store with TTL
- SDK helpers and examples in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript
- Add integration tests to eval-harness and redwood-quickstarts

Commits:
- "runtime: emit checkpoint frames at safe boundaries (checkpoint id + cursor + token)"
- "gateway: resume handshake endpoint and header parsing (X-Redwood-Resume)"
- "tooling: transient toolcall state and commit marker handling"
- "lease-store: persist checkpoint metadata with configurable ttl"
- "sdk(py/ts): helpers: StreamCheckpoint and Client.resume_from_checkpoint"
- "tests: e2e resume/cancel/duplicate-invoke prevention"

Files changed (high level):
- serving/runtime/streaming/checkpoint.go

- serving/tooling/toolcall_manager.go
- gateway/handlers/resume_handshake.go

Review conversation (high-level excerpts):
- Ava Morgan (review): "Excellent approach keeping the checkpoint small. One concern: TTL=24h might be surprising for customers — recommend exposing as config per org."
- Author (Diego): "Agreed, exposed as org-level config with infra default 24h; added CLI flag for private deployments."
- Lina Chen (review): "What about streaming latency overhead? Can we guarantee no extra round-trip on hot path?"
- Author: "We only emit checkpoints at existing boundary points or on background intervals; path for plain text streaming unchanged. Added benchmarks showing <1% mean p99 increase in hot paths."
- Marcus Boyd (safety): "Tool commit marker requirement is good. Need audit events for uncommitted tool attempts — added."
- CI bot: "flake8/linters passed, integration tests initially flaky on env; reran and passed."

CI summary: all unit and integration tests passed after second run. Perf bench: micro-benchmark shows 0.6% p99 latency increase for streams with checkpointing enabled; streams without checkpointing unaffected.

Merge outcome: merged via squash. Merge commit message: "streaming: checkpointing + resume handshake to preserve toolcall boundaries and prevent duplicate tool invocations (ENG-1894)".

Operational notes for rollout:
- Default: feature gated off for legacy hosted customers. New API header enables behavior. Gradual rollout plan described in rollout/2026-03-stream-checkpoint-plan.md.
- Add migration docs for customers using custom tool providers (must return commit marker)
- Add console dashboard: checkpoint/resume metrics and duplicate-invoke alarms

Release notes:
- Added optional streaming checkpoints and resume handshake to prevent duplicate tool/function invocations on cancel+resume and to preserve structured output integrity across reconnects. Opt-in via X-Redwood-Resume header or SDK helpers. See quickstarts/streaming-resume for sample usage.

Breaking change: false
